actions_or_findings.title: CURRENT_TASK_BLOCKER: Refresh can accept a revoked session after phone change
actions_or_findings.trigger: Refresh reads the session before phone change, waits for the user lock, then rereads it after phone change commits.
actions_or_findings.rationale: The first read places the session in SQLAlchemy’s identity map. The locked reread does not use populate_existing, so its ORM object can retain the old revoked_at value and issue a surviving successor. The race evidence exercises the opposite ordering. [SQLAlchemy documentation](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/queryguide/api.html) confirms that populate_existing is needed to refresh an already loaded instance.

actions_or_findings.title: CURRENT_TASK_BLOCKER: Logout retains a conflicting lock order
actions_or_findings.trigger: Logout locks an old session while phone change holds the user lock and tries to lock active sessions.
actions_or_findings.rationale: Logout then inserts an audit row whose actor_user_id foreign key needs a shared user-row lock. That creates a session-to-user versus user-to-session deadlock. If phone change is aborted, its OTPs have already been consumed. This lock inversion was introduced by the new user lock and session scan. [MySQL documentation](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-locks-set.html) describes the foreign-key shared locks.
